chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Abrash al-Kalbi asked him about the Words of Allah, Exalted and Majestic: 'The Day when the earth shall be Changed into a different earth'. He said: 'It would be turned into pure bread. The people would eat from it until they are free from the Reckoning'.

Al-Abrash said, 'I said, 'The people on that Day would be too pre-occupied from the eating'. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'They would be in the Fire, not being too pre-occupied from eating the thorny bushes and drinking the scalding water, and they would be in the Punishment, so how would they be too pre-occupied from it during the Reckoning?'.
ai.seo_question: What does the 'different earth' in Quran 14:48 refer to according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the 'different earth' in Surah Ibrahim as a specific, pure bread consumed by humanity during the Reckoning (Hisab), addressing the logical objection that people are too occupied with judgment to eat. He resolves this by distinguishing between the general busyness of the Hereafter and the specific, involuntary preoccupation of those in Hellfire with consuming thorny bushes (Zaqqum) and scalding water, which does not distract them from their accounting. This narration highlights the Shia exegetical approach of using contextual logic to reconcile apparent contradictions in eschatological descriptions.
